llm.gtx1660: Desktop GTX 1660 SUPER (Turing, 6 GB, no tensor cores), measured 16 Oct 2026 with the machine idle: qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M (3.3 GB weights, thinking off) sits 100 percent on the GPU (3.1 GB at a 4k context) and generates about 59 tokens per second, a 50-token patient reply taking about 1.0 s (p95 1.15 s); qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M (6.6 GB) does not fit and runs 57 percent on the GPU with the rest on the CPU, about 12 tokens per second and about 5 s for the same reply, so it is the offline batch model only. Speech recognition and the Unity Editor were not loaded in these runs; the laptop RTX 4050 is not measured.
llm.rtx4050: Laptop RTX 4050 (Ada, 6 GB, tensor cores, power-limited): faster per token than the desktop for the same model, but if Unity VR renders on this GPU the model must share VRAM with the scene; budget about 2 GB for a model while Unity runs, or run the model on the desktop.
llm.ram: 16 GB system RAM on the desktop limits CPU offload to small models; laptop RAM to be recorded in the benchmark.
llm.latency: Interactive replies: p95 under 3 s; generation stages: under 25 s or served from the pre-generated pool; offline jobs: no limit.
llm.deployment: Recommended split (to confirm by p1-ai-infrastructure-s02): inference service on the desktop GPU, Unity on the laptop GPU, over the local network. Single-machine mode: Qwen3.5 2B (to be benchmarked) or CPU inference plus the pool. Remote inference only for offline jobs, never with real personal data.

llm_offline.gtx1660: Runs as a batch job on the desktop; larger models (8B with offload) acceptable because time is not critical.
llm_offline.rtx4050: Batch job when Unity is not running.
llm_offline.ram: CPU offload uses system RAM; keep batch size small on 16 GB.
llm_offline.deployment: Offline CLI on either machine; results stored and versioned; optional remote GPU for large batches.

asr.gtx1660: faster-whisper small.en or medium.en with int8 is expected to fit beside a 4B LLM on the desktop (upstream lists large-v2 int8 at about 2.9 GB); exact VRAM to be measured.
asr.rtx4050: Possible, but competes with Unity rendering; prefer the desktop or CPU int8 small.en.
asr.ram: CPU fallback with small.en int8 on the Ryzen 5 2600 (6 cores) is expected to be near real time; to be measured.
asr.latency: Under 1.5 s from end of speech to text.
asr.deployment: Part of the inference service; push-to-talk audio streamed from Unity.

tts.latency: Under 0.5 s per sentence; fixed lines pre-rendered.
tts.deployment: Pre-rendered files shipped with Unity; live TTS in the inference service or on the Unity machine's CPU.

cpu.latency: Milliseconds to under 2 s per scenario.
cpu.deployment: Python generation service or offline tool; C# Core where it touches state.

classifier_small.gtx1660: Training a small encoder (about 66 to 110 million parameters) fits easily; inference on CPU in milliseconds.
classifier_small.deployment: Exported model (for example ONNX) in the inference service.

diffusion.gtx1660: Training an image-generation model of Stable Diffusion size is not practical on 6 GB; small mask-conditioned models at 128 to 256 px can be trained slowly; inference of a 1.5-class model in fp16 is borderline. To be measured.
diffusion.rtx4050: As the desktop, faster; never while Unity runs.
diffusion.ram: 16 GB is tight for data loading; stream from disk.
diffusion.latency: Offline only: images are generated in batches, reviewed by metrics, and stored as labelled synthetic assets; never generated during a session.
diffusion.deployment: Offline research pipeline; a rented or institutional GPU for training if the local run is too slow.

finetune.gtx1660: QLoRA of a 1.7B model is expected to fit; 4B is borderline on 6 GB and must be measured; no tensor cores, so slow.
finetune.rtx4050: Faster QLoRA for 1.7B to 4B; never while Unity runs.
finetune.latency: Offline training; served adapters add no runtime cost.
finetune.deployment: Offline; adapter weights versioned with their evaluation report; remote GPU if local training is too slow.

novelty_spec.meaning: Fresh means a coherent, evidence-informed combination this trainee has not met; it never means random values.

fields: block ids for PRES, CMB, RSK, ALG, MED, EVT slots

novelty_spec.distance: D = sum over levels of weight x (1 - Jaccard(level sets)); weighted Jaccard where items carry weights
accept_when: D >= 0.35 against each of the trainee's last 10 sessions
structural level not identical to any of the last 3 sessions
deliberate-practice requests may repeat the structural level if the clinical level differs (clinical distance >= 0.3)
novelty_spec.library_check: report the distance to the nearest library case; an exact structural copy of a library case is allowed only when the pool cannot satisfy the objectives
metrics: novelty rate (share of sessions meeting the threshold)
block-space coverage per trainee over time
novelty_spec.fallback: after 5 attempts serve the most novel valid candidate and log LOW_NOVELTY
reproducibility: package id = SHA-256 of canonical(request, seed, pack versions, block library version, prompt version, model digest, content manifest hash)
named seed streams per stage and slot (seed/stage/slot) so adding a slot does not shift other values
LLM output is stored in the package; replay never calls the model; regenerating without the stored output can change only narrative fields

assumptions: Generated scenarios are practice-only (review status GENERATED_PRACTICE_ONLY); assessment keeps fixed cases.
Clinician sign-off is not a development gate (policy 12 Oct 2026); automated validation is the gate and clinician answers are welcome research input.

Hardware: two 6 GB GPUs, a desktop GTX 1660 SUPER (measured: 16 GB RAM, Ryzen 5 2600) and a laptop RTX 4050 (RAM and CPU to be recorded, DT-118); Ollama is not installed (checked 12 Oct 2026) and installation is a roadmap task (PH-20), not a reason to drop a feature.
Latency targets are estimates until the benchmark (OQ-01).
Raw restricted data never enters the repository; only aggregates and selected licensed images.

nodes.description: The trainee (or the trainer) asks for a session in Unity or the CLI. Today the CLI `run` and `next-case` commands start a session on an existing case; a request for a freshly generated case is planned.

nodes.label: Fallback: pooled or library case
nodes.description: When generation cannot deliver a valid, novel case in budget, a validated package from the pre-generated pool or a case from the existing library is loaded instead. The trainee never sees an unvalidated case.

nodes.label: Normal versus abnormal profiling per modality
nodes.description: Describe each modality before any generator is designed: distribution of normal values, abnormal patterns per condition, borderline zones, missingness, artefacts, correlations. Lab percentiles, vital-sign noise and ECG templates already exist as aggregates; the per-condition profiles, correlations and the written analysis do not.

nodes.label: Generator parameter packs (versioned)
nodes.description: Turn the profiles into small versioned JSON packs the live generators read: per analyte and condition a distribution (band, centre, spread, skew, truncation), correlation matrices for linked analytes, vital-sign trajectories, ECG rhythm parameters, artefact rates. Live sessions only read packs; they never refit or retrain.

nodes.label: Model preparation: pull, quantise, benchmark (no training)
nodes.description: Download the candidate served models, record their digests and licences, and benchmark latency, VRAM and structured-output validity on this hardware. Nothing is trained here.

nodes.label: Prompt and schema registry
nodes.description: Versioned prompts and JSON schemas for every model call (composition, dialogue, debrief, classifier, judge). A prompt change is a content change: new version, new evaluation run.

nodes.label: Session request
nodes.description: Unity or the CLI asks for a session: trainee pseudonym, mode (practice only for generated cases), scenario family (S1 or S2), optional focus competencies, level, seed (optional; drawn and logged if absent), time budget.
nodes.component: server/generation/request.py (planned); today: CLI flags --level --variant --noise and next-case
nodes.method: Schema validation of the request; assessment mode is refused for generated content.
nodes.validation: JSON schema; mode guard.
nodes.acceptance: Every request is either accepted with a logged seed or rejected with a reason; no request reaches LG-02 without a seed.
nodes.error_handling: Invalid request: 400 with field errors. Assessment mode with generation: 409, serve a fixed assessment case instead.

nodes.label: Learning objectives and difficulty target
nodes.description: Turn the trainee's history into objectives: the weakest behaviours and dimensions from the Elo ratings, the target difficulty, the competencies to exercise, and what must not repeat (recent fingerprints).
outputs: Objectives v1: target competencies, difficulty vector over 8 dimensions, exclusions
nodes.method: Deterministic: reuse the Elo ratings (K 16, 3 sessions before adapting) and dimension mapping. An LLM is not used to choose objectives (choice must be explainable and reproducible).
nodes.validation: Every objective names a behaviour or dimension that exists in content.
tests: objective derivation unit tests against fixed histories
nodes.acceptance: Same history and seed give the same objectives.
nodes.error_handling: No history: use the beginner default objectives for the family.

nodes.label: Context retrieval
nodes.description: Retrieve the evidence the scenario may draw on: candidate blocks matching the objectives, reference cases with similar structure, bands and critical limits for the conditions involved, what-ifs, events, and the SR ids behind each.
outputs: RetrievedContext: ranked blocks, reference cases, bands, SR ids
nodes.method: Tag filter then BM25 ranking (deterministic). Embedding retrieval only if measured recall is below 0.9 on the retrieval evaluation set.
nodes.validation: Every retrieved item is APPROVED_FOR_TRAINING or above, or labelled generated-practice-only.
tests: recall@k on the retrieval evaluation set
nodes.acceptance: Recall@20 at least 0.9 on the evaluation set; zero items below the allowed review status.
nodes.error_handling: Empty retrieval for an objective: drop that objective with a logged reason; if all drop, use the family template.

nodes.label: AI scenario plan composition and constraint solving
nodes.description: The AI composer (LLM with retrieval over the scenario knowledge base and exemplar cases, schema-constrained to approved ids) proposes a ScenarioPlan: problems, comorbidities, investigations with expected findings, decision points and traps, events, branches, outcomes and a rationale per choice. The deterministic solver completes missing slots and enforces requires/excludes, KB relations, difficulty bounds and novelty. With no model available the solver alone produces the plan (baseline and fallback). Revised 12 Oct 2026 (second pass): previously solver-only selection.
outputs: ComponentSet: block ids per slot, solver trace
nodes.method: LLM + retrieval proposes the plan (MC-01, JSON schema); seeded constraint solver completes and checks it (backtracking over slots with requires/excludes, KB relations, difficulty bounds, novelty pre-filter).
nodes.validation: Constraint re-check after selection; solver trace stored in the package.
tests: property test: no output violates requires/excludes
nodes.acceptance: Zero constraint violations over 10,000 seeds; unsatisfiable inputs end in a logged fallback.
nodes.error_handling: Unsatisfiable: relax optional slots in a fixed order, then fall back to FALLBACK-POOL-LIBRARY.

nodes.label: Scenario skeleton
nodes.description: Assemble the chosen blocks into a case-file-shaped skeleton: patient slots, problems with their discovery rules, investigation orders that must exist, expected end state, clock, events and handover items. Every clinical value is still a slot, not a number.
nodes.method: Deterministic assembly from block templates.
nodes.validation: case_file.schema.json with slots allowed; every problem has a discovery rule.
nodes.acceptance: Every skeleton validates against the schema and every problem is discoverable.
nodes.error_handling: Schema violation: defect report to LG-12.

nodes.label: AI composition (narrative, patient profile, persona)
nodes.description: A served LLM fills the narrative slots only: presenting story in the patient's words, social context, persona traits, staff handover wording, distractor texture. It returns JSON that must match a schema whose enums are the allowed block ids and tags. It never chooses a value, a diagnosis, a drug or a result.
inputs: ScenarioSkeleton (values hidden where they are hidden facts)
nodes.method: LLM with JSON-schema constrained output (Ollama `format`), temperature 0.7 to 0.8, thinking off; prompt and model digest logged.
nodes.validation: JSON schema, grounding validator (no invented drug, value, diagnosis or hidden fact), lexicon checks.
tests: T-SA1 to T-SA4 (enum schema rejects invented ids)
nodes.acceptance: At least 95 percent schema-valid on first try on the benchmark set; zero grounding failures reach the package; template fallback always available.
nodes.error_handling: Timeout (budget 25 s), invalid JSON, schema failure or grounding failure: one retry with the defect as an avoid-hint, then the template narrative (deterministic fallback).

nodes.label: Numeric generation (labs, vitals, trends)
nodes.description: Fill every numeric slot: lab results per analyte conditioned on the case's conditions, vital-sign baselines and trajectories, repeat results and trends. Values come from the parameter packs (OFF-03): truncated distributions inside the band the block demands, joint sampling of linked analytes, seeded per slot. Today lab values are drawn inside verified bands (EXP-DATA-2, 10,000 seeds); conditioning and correlation are planned.
outputs: numeric results with band, flag, units and provenance
nodes.method: Statistical (seeded truncated normal or log-normal per band, Gaussian copula for linked analytes), never an LLM.
nodes.validation: Band check, unit check, plausibility table (content/lab_plausibility.csv), critical-limit consistency, cross-analyte rules.
nodes.acceptance: 100 percent of values within the demanded band over 10,000 seeds; generated marginals within the profile's p5 to p95 for normal slots; same seed gives identical values.
nodes.error_handling: A value outside the demanded band or an impossible combination: redraw the slot (bounded 20), then clamp to the band edge and log.

nodes.label: Image and waveform handling (ECG, ultrasound, X-ray, CT)
nodes.description: Pick, for every imaging and ECG slot, an asset whose finding tags match the skeleton (real first, labelled synthetic where no real image exists, ADR-0003 and ADR-0004); for ECG also allow a seeded rhythm variant (rate, noise) from the PTB-XL templates or a NeuroKit2 ecgsyn trace. The written report comes from the asset's approved report template, filled with the case's values.
outputs: asset references with dataset id, licence, finding tags, report text
nodes.method: Retrieval from the labelled library (deterministic, seeded tie-break) plus seeded parametric ECG variation. No diffusion or GAN image generation at runtime (E64 is a deferred offline research track, PH-24).
nodes.validation: Finding tags of the asset equal the skeleton's findings; report numbers equal the numeric slots; licence allows the use.
nodes.acceptance: Zero tag mismatches; every asset has a licence row.
nodes.error_handling: No asset with the needed tags: choose the written-only result if the test allows one; otherwise defect to LG-12 (change the block).

nodes.label: Cross-modal consistency
nodes.description: Check that every modality tells the same story: ECG rhythm against pulse and monitor; ultrasound findings against inflammatory markers and examination; free air on X-ray against peritonism; potassium against ECG changes; haemolysed sample against the repeat; sepsis tier against vitals and lactate; pregnancy test against sex and age; timeline order against the clock.
outputs: consistency report (pass or defects with rule ids)
nodes.method: Deterministic rule table (VR-CM rules); an LLM judge may flag suspected inconsistencies as advisory only (LG-11).
nodes.validation: Rule table itself has tests with one passing and one failing example per rule.
tests: one positive and one negative fixture per cross-modal rule
mutation set extended with cross-modal breaks
nodes.acceptance: Every cross-modal mutation in the evaluation set is caught.
nodes.error_handling: Each defect names the slots involved and goes to LG-12.

nodes.label: Constraint and clinical-safety validation (Stage B)
nodes.description: Run the existing Stage B checks (11 ordered checks, 12 contradiction types) and the Core ContentGate on the full package. Checks 9 and 10 need a golden run: for generated cases the solver's correct-path script is executed headless by the Core.
nodes.component: tools/composer/stage_b.py (exists) + Core ContentGate (exists) + headless correct-path run (planned)
nodes.method: Deterministic validator; the AI cannot mark anything approved.
nodes.validation: 60 of 60 mutation cases rejected today; extended set for generated content.
tests: headless correct-path reaches the expected end state
nodes.acceptance: Zero packages with a Stage B defect are delivered; the correct path reaches the declared end state.
nodes.error_handling: Defects go to LG-12; three failed repair rounds end in FALLBACK-POOL-LIBRARY.

nodes.label: Quality evaluation
nodes.description: Score a valid scenario for teaching quality: objective coverage, difficulty match, discoverability of every problem, distractor fairness, narrative coherence, reading level, persona consistency. Deterministic metrics decide; an LLM judge with a fixed rubric gives advisory scores that are logged and compared against human ratings offline.
outputs: QualityReport: metric scores, judge scores, verdict
nodes.method: Deterministic metrics (gate) + LLM-as-judge rubric with JSON output (advisory only).
nodes.validation: Judge agreement with human ratings measured offline (target Spearman 0.6 or more before the judge may influence repair).
nodes.acceptance: Quality gate rejects all gold 'poor' scenarios and passes 90 percent of gold 'good' ones.
data_dependencies: OFF-07 gold scenarios with human ratings
nodes.error_handling: Below threshold: defects to LG-12; judge unavailable: deterministic metrics only (logged).

nodes.label: Repair, regeneration or rejection
nodes.description: Fix defects at the cheapest level: redraw a numeric slot, swap an asset, swap a block, re-ask the LLM with the defect as an avoid-hint. Bounded: at most 3 repair rounds and the session time budget. Every repair is logged in the package's provenance.
inputs: defect list from LG-09, LG-10, LG-11, LG-13
outputs: repaired candidate (back to the failing stage) or rejection
nodes.method: Deterministic repair strategy table; LLM re-ask only for narrative defects.
nodes.validation: A repaired candidate repeats every check from the earliest stage it changed.
tests: repair strategy tests per defect type
nodes.acceptance: No repaired candidate skips a check; budget is never exceeded.
nodes.error_handling: Budget exhausted: FALLBACK-POOL-LIBRARY with the defect log kept for the evaluation loop.

nodes.label: Novelty check (fingerprint)
nodes.description: Build the structured fingerprint (structural, clinical and surface levels) and compare it with this trainee's recent sessions and the library. Novel means a coherent combination the trainee has not met, not random noise.
nodes.method: Weighted Jaccard over fingerprint sets, MinHash LSH (datasketch, MIT) for fast nearest-neighbour search when histories grow.
nodes.validation: Fingerprint schema; thresholds documented in the live generation spec.
nodes.acceptance: Structural distance at least 0.35 from each of the trainee's last 10 sessions in at least 95 percent of sessions where the pool allows it.
nodes.error_handling: Not novel: defect to LG-12 (swap a block); after 5 attempts accept the most novel valid candidate and log low novelty.

nodes.label: Packaging with provenance
nodes.description: Write the Scenario Package: case file, generated values, asset references, narrative, solver trace, fingerprint, quality and novelty reports, seed, pack versions, prompt versions, model digests, content manifest hash, review status GENERATED_PRACTICE_ONLY, package SHA-256.
nodes.method: Deterministic serialisation with canonical JSON ordering.
nodes.validation: Package schema; hash recomputed on load.
nodes.acceptance: Same inputs give a byte-identical package.
nodes.error_handling: Serialisation error: reject and fall back.

nodes.label: Unity integration
nodes.description: Unity fetches the package (or reads one from the pre-generated pool on disk), the C# loader validates schema, hash and review status, then starts a Core Session on it. Unity code is not modified in this planning task.
nodes.method: Deterministic loader; offline pool when the backend is unreachable.
nodes.validation: ContentGate in the Core (exists) extended for GENERATED_PRACTICE_ONLY.
tests: EditMode test: package loads into a Session
nodes.acceptance: A pooled package loads offline in under 2 s on the target PC.
nodes.error_handling: Download failure or hash mismatch: load the next pooled package or a library case.

nodes.label: Live simulation
nodes.description: The deterministic Core runs the case: SimClock in 0.5 s steps, subsystems, LitePhysio, EventDirector (seeded draw in practice), discovery, sepsis, clashes. Generated cases run on exactly the same engine as library cases.
outputs: state changes, observable state, session log
nodes.component: src/ProcSense.Core (Session, ISubsystem pipeline, SimClock, LitePhysio, EventDirector)
nodes.method: Deterministic simulation; replay hash.
nodes.validation: Replay hash equality; golden runs.
nodes.acceptance: Replay of every session reproduces its log hash.
nodes.error_handling: Content exception stops the session with a logged reason.

nodes.label: Action interpretation
nodes.description: Turn what the trainee did into structured actions: VR interactions and menu choices map deterministically; free speech goes ASR then the communication-act extractor (LLM, P1) to a structured act with confidence. Low-confidence or critical acts are never credited from the model alone.
outputs: SimAction (verb, target, channel, params) or CommAct with confidence
nodes.method: Deterministic mapping; ASR (faster-whisper); LLM act extraction with enum schema; P2 small trained classifier.
nodes.validation: Enum schema; critical-act guard in the evidence store (exists).
tests: classifier macro-F1 on the frozen split
nodes.acceptance: Classifier stays switched off below macro-F1 0.75.
nodes.error_handling: Low confidence: ask the trainee to repeat or choose from a menu; model down: menu only.

nodes.label: Deterministic state update and scoring
nodes.description: Rules decide every state change, every credit and penalty, the outcome and the fail gate (ADR-0005). AI output can only be evidence the rules weigh, never a decision.
nodes.method: Deterministic rules and rubric (22 behaviours).
nodes.validation: Scoring tests; check_report.py.
nodes.acceptance: Same log gives the same score.
nodes.error_handling: Unknown action: logged and ignored.

nodes.label: Grounded debrief
nodes.description: Template debrief from DebriefFacts is always produced first (built). An LLM may rewrite it for tone and coaching; the grounding validator rejects any dropped fact, changed number, flipped verdict or invented event and the template is shown instead.
nodes.method: Deterministic template + LLM rewrite behind the validator.
nodes.validation: Grounding validator (Python and C# twin, 44 shared vectors).
nodes.acceptance: Zero validator escapes on the mutation set.
nodes.error_handling: Model down or validator failure: template only.

nodes.label: Session history
nodes.description: Store the pseudonymised session record: scores, ratings update, fingerprint of the generated case, package hash, debrief facts. Feeds the next session's objectives and novelty check.
nodes.component: record-session CLI (exists); backend sessions store (planned p1-backend-s02)
nodes.method: Deterministic append-only store.
nodes.validation: History schema; no real names (pseudonym only).
nodes.acceptance: Every completed session has exactly one history entry.
nodes.error_handling: Store unavailable: write locally, sync later.

nodes.label: Evaluation feedback loop (offline only)
nodes.description: Aggregate rejection reasons, repair rates, novelty, quality scores, trainee outcomes and validator escapes across sessions. Results update parameter packs, block weights, prompts and thresholds in a reviewed offline release, never inside a live session.
outputs: proposed pack, prompt and threshold changes
nodes.method: Deterministic aggregation; optional LLM summarisation of defect clusters (advisory).
nodes.validation: Changes go through the normal content build, --check and CI.
tests: report generation test on fixture logs
nodes.acceptance: Every pack or prompt change cites the evaluation report that motivated it.
nodes.error_handling: n/a (offline)

nodes.label: Scenario knowledge base construction (A66)
nodes.description: Typed relations (condition-finding, test-finding, decision-consequence, interactions) imported from verified tables, extracted by an LLM from case files and the walkthrough (quote-checked, reviewed) and quantified from dataset profiles with n and confidence.
nodes.component: tools/kb/build_kb.py, tools/kb/extract_relations.py (built; extraction precision 0.8 on 100 hand-labelled relations not yet measured: needs a labeller, DT-114)
blockers: precision of the model extraction needs 100 hand-labelled relations (a person, p1-ai-infrastructure-s04)

nodes.label: Learner profile retrieval (session start)
nodes.description: Load the trainee's LearnerProfile v1 (posteriors, demonstrated weaknesses, hypotheses, trends, recent fingerprints).

nodes.label: Personalised targeting policy
nodes.description: Turn the profile into Objectives v1 (rules, later a contextual bandit adopted after off-policy evaluation) and the why-this-case facts.

nodes.label: Learner profile update (post-session, cheap)
nodes.description: Extract SessionEvidence v1, update posteriors and pattern status; the LLM interpreter adds hypotheses offline. No model retraining in a session.

nodes.label: Core engine (Session, ISubsystem pipeline, SimClock, replay)
nodes.description: Core engine (Session, ISubsystem pipeline, SimClock, replay). Where: src/ProcSense.Core/Session.cs, Replay/. Tests: 17 P0 goldens, replay hash.

nodes.label: LitePhysio and display zones
nodes.description: LitePhysio and display zones. Where: src/ProcSense.Core/Physiology/. Tests: physiology tests.

validation_rules.rule: Normal values lie inside the reference band and inside the dataset profile p5 to p95 for the population.
Abnormal values lie in the band the block demands (mild, moderate, significant, critical) and agree with critical_results limits.
Borderline values are within one band-width step of a band edge and are labelled borderline so scoring does not treat them as definite.
A missing result is only allowed where the block declares it (sample not sent, lab delay) and must have a visible reason in the EMR.
Artefacts (haemolysis, motion, lead-off) come with their recognisable cue and a resolution path (repeat, recheck).
Deliberate conflicting data (old note versus wristband) must be teaching blocks with a discoverable cue; accidental conflicts are defects.
Physiologically impossible values or combinations (lab_plausibility.csv, units) are always defects.
Deliberate educational anomalies are labelled in the package and in the debrief and are never shown in assessment mode.
ECG rhythm and rate agree with the pulse, the monitor trace and the examination (AF means an irregular pulse).
Potassium in the significant band or above is accompanied by an ECG consistent with it or by a stated reason it is not.
Ultrasound cholecystitis findings agree with inflammatory markers and right upper quadrant findings.
Free air on the chest film agrees with peritonism and the perforation block.
Sepsis tier agrees with vitals, NEWS2 and lactate.
A haemolysed potassium has a normal or explained repeat and a sample comment.
Pregnancy test exists only where sex and age allow; result agrees with the profile.
Event times are ordered and consistent with the clock and turnaround times.
The narrative never states a value, drug or diagnosis absent from the structured case (grounding validator).
No prescribed or suggested medicine belongs to an allergy group unless the block teaches that clash.
The pipeline JSON parses and has every required top-level field.
Node, edge, group, dataset, model, phase, rule, fallback and question ids are unique within their list.
Every edge source and target is a node id.
Every referenced id (group, model, dataset, task, phase, feature, node) exists.
Every feature is realised by at least one node and mapped to at least one task in a phase.
Every live stage is reachable from an entry node and can reach an exit node.
Every cycle in the data-flow graph passes through an edge marked as a documented cycle.

Every feature has a complete implementation plan: all plan fields, the seven AI questions, separate capability plans with schemas, flow, validation, five-case failure handling, tests, metrics, baseline, acceptance and both-GPU hardware notes, and tasks that exist and sit in a phase.
Every node and edge traces to feature plans or plan step files that exist; plan documents cite only ids that exist in the JSON.
Nothing planned is labelled implemented: an implemented node or feature must list evidence paths that exist in the repository.
